items.title: Hybrid Spark: Adaptive Speculative Decoding That Lets the Content Choose the Drafter
items.summary: Speculative decoding (SD) speeds up large language model (LLM) serving, but its gain depends on the workload's \emph{shape}, such as batch size and context length, and on its \emph{content}. A model-based drafter proposes a short block on any content, while a model-free drafter such as n-gram lookup proposes long copies at almost no cost when the output repeats its input, as in code editing. Adaptive verification spends a batch-wide verification budget on the draft tokens most likely to be accepted, but it supports only one model-based drafter. Model-free drafters provide no per-token confidence, so they cannot take part in budget allocation, and deployments must either fix one drafter or split their GPUs between drafters. We present \sys, a framework that runs a model-based and a model-free drafter on every step and gives each request the better of their chains, within adaptive verification and entirely on the GPU, which keeps asynchronous scheduling intact. The key idea is a price per verified draft token: the goodput that slot would earn elsewhere in the batch. Once the model-free drafter's tokens carry calibrated acceptance estimates, fit once on general text, this price puts both drafters' chains on one scale. Instantiated with \dspark and an n-gram drafter in vLLM, \sys achieves 1.10--1.62\x the output throughput of \dspark on code editing at batch size~4 and 1.04--1.27\x at batch size~128, while staying at 0.97--1.01\x of it on chat at temperature~0. A single deployment can therefore serve both workloads.

items.title: Speculative Decoding: Exploiting Speculative Execution for Accelerating Seq2seq Generation
items.summary: We propose Speculative Decoding (SpecDec), for the first time ever, to formally study exploiting the idea of speculative execution to accelerate autoregressive (AR) decoding. Speculative Decoding has two innovations: Spec-Drafter -- an independent model specially optimized for efficient and accurate drafting -- and Spec-Verification -- a reliable method for verifying the drafted tokens efficiently in the decoding paradigm. Experimental results on various seq2seq tasks including machine translation and abstractive summarization show our approach can achieve around $5\times$ speedup for the popular Transformer architectures with comparable generation quality to beam search decoding, refreshing the impression that the draft-then-verify paradigm introduces only $1.4\times$$\sim$$2\times$ speedup. In addition to the remarkable speedup, we also demonstrate 3 additional advantages of SpecDec, revealing its practical value for accelerating generative models in real-world applications. Our models and codes are available at https://github.com/hemingkx/SpecDec.

items.title: Component-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding in Hybrid Language Models
items.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive inference by drafting candidate tokens with a fast model and verifying them in parallel with the target. Self-speculative methods avoid the need for an external drafter but have been studied exclusively in homogeneous Transformer architectures. We introduce component-aware self-speculative decoding, the first method to exploit the internal architectural heterogeneity of hybrid language models, isolating the SSM/linear-attention subgraph as a zero-cost internal draft. We evaluate this on two architecturally distinct hybrid families: Falcon-H1 (parallel: Mamba-2 + attention per layer) and Qwen3.5 (sequential: interleaved linear and attention layers), with a pure Transformer control (Qwen2.5). Parallel hybrids achieve acceptance rates of alpha = 0.68 at draft length k=2 under greedy decoding, while sequential hybrids yield only alpha = 0.038 -- an 18x gap attributable to how each architecture integrates its components. The property is scale-invariant: Falcon-H1 at 3B reproduces the rates observed at 0.5B. We further show that perplexity degradation from a companion ablation study predicts speculative viability without running speculative decoding: a 3.15x ratio (Falcon) maps to alpha = 0.37 at k=4, while 81.96x (Qwen) maps to alpha = 0.019. For sequential hybrids, generic LayerSkip achieves 12x higher acceptance rates than the component-aware strategy. The composition pattern of hybrid models -- not merely the presence of alternative components -- determines whether component-level self-speculation is viable.

items.title: OpenAI promised developers six months’ notice. GPT-4o users got three. - The New Stack
items.summary:
GPT-4o arrived on May 13, 2024, as OpenAI’s flagship and built a following loyal enough to change the company’s plans. When GPT-5 replaced it in August 2025, Reddit filled with complaints, and OpenAI brought it back for paying ChatGPT subscribers the very next day. That reprieve lasted until February 13, 2026, when GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 disappeared from ChatGPT. Both remained available through the API, but that access now is sunsetting. [...] By then, OpenAI said just 0.1% of daily ChatGPT users were still choosing GPT-4o, although the model continued serving API requests for applications built around it.

GPT-4.1 was a different kind of release, arriving on April 14, 2025, as an API-only family that skipped ChatGPT entirely and went straight after developers with stronger coding, better instruction following, room for up to a million tokens of context, and more reliable diff formats for anyone letting a model loose on large files. [...] Featued image for: OpenAI promised developers six months’ notice. GPT-4o users got three.

OpenAI is retiring four GPT-4 models from its API on January 14, 2027. The deprecation notice the company sent developers Wednesday covers GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1, and GPT-4.1 mini, along with their dated snapshots and every fine-tuned model built on top of them.

items.title: Introducing GPTZero 4o
items.summary:
We are launching GPTZero 4o, O standing for Omni: a model that leads not only in AI detection, but also in mixed and modified AI text – and is versatile across different writing styles, as well as different model types, including Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Grok, and DeepSeek. In short, it’s our most accurate model yet, with a false positive rate of only 1 in 10,402 on diverse student writing corpra, and it outperforms competitors across major 3rd party benchmarks. [...] ## Conclusion

GPTZero 4o is our most accurate model yet, and most importantly, it demonstrates how we have a system we’ll keep improving over time. By expanding our training data and testing against challenging benchmarks, we know we can continue to improve how we address the trickier cases of AI-generated text detection. [...] The PERSUADE dataset is a set of student-written essays that was collected to improve writing feedback algorithms. While collecting the dataset, the authors also annotated student demographic information including gender, English Language Learner status, race/ethnicity, economic disadvantages, disability status, and grade level.

items.title: OpenAI's own page still calls GPT-4o its flagship, and it leaves the API on January 14
items.summary:
OpenAI's own image of a coding workflow in ChatGPT. Software that calls GPT-4o or GPT-4.1 has until January 14, 2027 to point somewhere else. Image: OpenAI

GPT-4o's own model page now carries a Deprecated badge and still introduces the model as "our versatile, high-intelligence flagship model" and "the best model for most tasks". It publishes no shutdown date of its own. [...] All four retiring models point at a single successor, gpt-6-luna, which OpenAI prices at $0.10 per million input tokens, $0.01 per million cached input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens. GPT-4o lists $2.50, $1.25 and $10 for the same three lines, so the newer model costs a 25th as much on input and a 20th on output. [...] OpenAI will remove GPT-4o from its API on January 14, 2027, together with GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini. OpenAI says it notified developers using the four models on October 14, 2026, which leaves 92 days between the notice and the switch-off, where the same page sets a floor of six months for a generally available model.

items.title: OpenAI Suit Says GPT-4o Practiced Medicine Without a License - FourWeekMBA
items.summary: Gennaro Cuofano is a CRO and tech executive who has worked in AI since late 2015, starting with bringing NLP, natural-language generation, voice and chatbot products to the marketing industry. His background is in law and finance: he holds a Master's degree in Law and an International MBA with an emphasis on corporate finance (LUISS Business School and the University of San Diego, 2012), and worked as a financial analyst at a real-estate investment firm in San Diego and as an assistant [...] The New York Times reported on 27 October 2026 that the parents of Bowen Wan, a 31-year-old Amazon software engineer with epilepsy, had sued OpenAI and its chief executive Sam Altman. Their complaint, filed that day in the Superior Court of California, City and County of San Francisco, alleges that ChatGPT, running the GPT-4o model, practiced medicine without a license by designing a day-by-day schedule that tapered her stable 400-milligram dose of the anti-seizure drug lamotrigine to zero over [...] The eight causes of action in Wan v. OpenAI, grouped by us: five are the claims that a declaration filed for OpenAI on 7 April 2026 said each coordinated GPT-4o complaint asserts (strict product liability for design defect and failure to warn, negligence for design defect and failure to warn, and Unfair Competition Law); one is negligence through the unlawful practice of medicine and psychology; two are wrongful death and a survival action.
